The `types/index.d.ts` is a module since it has imports and exports. TypeScript doesn't seem to pick up global declarations from `.d.ts` files that are modules (but, it still picks up module augmentations). So if I do something like this in my TS files in a Next app:
```
if (process.env.NODE_ENV === 'production') {...}
```
TypeScript won't be able to infer that `NODE_ENV` is `'development' | 'production'`, since it doesn't use the `ProcessEnv` declaration from the Next's `index.d.ts`.
I think, the solution would be to create another file in the Next's folder (e.g. globals.d.ts) and store such declarations as `NodeJS.ProcessEnv` override in there.
